answer: Reputation is a scarce, unforgeable resource earned by consistently passing originality checks, and the economy spends it to filter out Sybil clusters before they can compound into a majority. The reason this works is that the attacker must pay a real cost on every identity, so scale becomes a liability rather than an advantage. This means an attacker must choose: either run a few high-quality identities, or many worthless ones — and neither option beats honest participation. Consider a quartz as the anchor of the cost.
